title: Archipelago Biotech — Model decision & deployment options
summary: Introductory discovery focused on model selection (open models), context-length needs, multilingual support, and deployment mode tradeoffs (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). Customer emphasized compliance (SOC2, KMS), latency SLOs for interactive UI, and cost sensitivity. Agreed next steps: share benchmark template, security pack, and schedule a dedicated latency/quantization deep-dive with infra team.
topics: tool-calling and function calls (retrieval + DB writes)
deployment mode: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC, on-prem)
security: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM, audit logs
performance targets: p95 latency, throughput, batching and quantization

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-05
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Riley Tran (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Diane Koh (Archipelago), Marcus Velez (Archipelago), Ellen Park (Archipelago CISO), Samir Gupta (Archipelago PM)

[00:00] Riley: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro from our side — I'm Riley, AE on the account. Priya's our SE, she'll drive the model/bench stuff.
[00:18] Diane: Hi, I'm Diane, head of data science at Archipelago, we build clinical summarization and triage workflows, lots of structured and unstructured notes.
[00:28] Marcus: Marcus — platform eng, I'll look at ops and networking.
[00:34] Ellen: Ellen, CISO, security and compliance.
[00:40] Riley: Awesome. High level — you sent the doc with goals: interactive UI with p95 latency under ~250ms for short completions, long-document summarization for whole visit bundles (32k-100k context), multilingual support (EN/ES/CN), and tool-calling to hit downstream systems. Is that right?
[00:55] Diane: Yep, that's the gist. For triage UI we need snappy responses, for batch summarization we need long context and high fidelity. Cost is a factor — we run millions of tokens a month.
[01:12] Priya: Cool. Quick question on scale — you said millions, can you ballpark tokens per day?
[01:22] Samir: Right now staging is about 5M tokens/day, production target 20M tokens/day in next 6 months if pilot goes well.
[01:32] Priya: That's helpful. For model selection, are you considering closed models or leaning open?
[01:39] Diane: We're trying to stay open where possible for auditability and cost. We looked at Llama-family, Mistral, and Falcon. We also saw some of the hybrid hosted offerings from Anthropic/OpenAI but want control.
[01:52] Riley: Makes sense. Two axes to consider: cost/latency (smaller quantized LLMs or 4-bit) and capability/context length. For long-docs you'll want models that either natively support 64k+ windows or use retrieval + chunking.
[02:08] Ellen: From a compliance perspective we need SOC2, ability to rotate keys (KMS/HSM), SAML SSO, and audit logs for data access. On-prem is preferred if cloud logs can't be retained by us.
[02:24] Riley: Understood. Redwood Private can be deployed in a VPC or on-prem packaging; we support customer KMS integrations and audit logs. We'll share the security pack.
[02:35] Marcus: What's the difference between Dedicated and Private here? Latency and data residency?
[02:42] Priya: Dedicated is reserved, single-tenant capacity in our cloud — predictable throughput and isolation. Private gives you the control plane in your VPC or on-prem, so your data never leaves your network. For many customers Dedicated is enough, but for strict regs Private is chosen.
[02:57] Marcus: Got it. For our compliance team, Ellen, is Dedicated acceptable?
[03:03] Ellen: Possibly, but only if we can enforce KMS/HSM with customer-owned keys and host in our chosen cloud region. We'll need to review the architecture diagram.
[03:12] Riley: We'll include that.
[03:16] Diane: Back to models, we've run some internal tests — Llama2-70B gives good accuracy but costs more; Mistral seems efficient; Falcon 180B performed well on benchmarks but we haven't tested 64k windows.
[03:32] Priya: A few notes — Mistral and the recent Llama variants have good perf/cost tradeoffs, but long context support varies. Some vendors stitch long context using sliding windows or retrieval-augmented generation, others have native 64k/128k context models. Redwood's runtime supports kernel selection and large context kernels where model supports it. For very long visit bundles we typically recommend a hybrid: retrieval chunking + KV caching for session state to keep latency down.
[03:58] Diane: We prefer fewer moving parts, but accuracy at the end is most important for summarization.
[04:05] Priya: Totally. For a pilot we could try two tracks: 1) native long-context model evaluation (e.g., 64k-capable model) and 2) retrieval + 32k model with optimized chunking and KV caching to see cost/latency trade-offs.
[04:20] Samir: That sounds good. How do you handle tool-calling? We need the model to call internal scoring services and also to write back to our triage queue.
[04:30] Riley: Redwood supports structured function-calling and tool integrations — you can pipe outputs to internal HTTP endpoints or run safe adapters. We also offer a sandbox for testing tool calls before production.
[04:41] Marcus: Any limitations on streaming + function-calls?
[04:45] Priya: Streaming and tool-calling are supported together, but with caveats: for complex multi-step transactions we recommend idempotency tokens and server-side orchestration. We'll demo patterns.
[04:58] Ellen: Encryption in transit and at rest? Key rotation?
[05:02] Riley: TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest, and support for customer-managed KMS/HSM. We'll send the key management doc.
[05:12] Diane: We care about multilingual accuracy, esp. medical Spanish and Mandarin. Any model recommendations?
[05:19] Priya: Mistral derivations and Llama2 variants have decent multilingual performance; for medical domain you may need fine-tuning or instruction tuning on in-domain examples. We can run evals with your Spanish/Mandarin notes to compare.
[05:31] Diane: Fine-tuning is doable but we'd prefer to avoid heavy ops. Can Redwood host fine-tuning or do we self-host?
[05:39] Riley: We have managed fine-tune workflows for Hosted customers; for Dedicated/Private we can provide tooling and help run ephemeral fine-tune workloads or LoRA-style adaptors.
[05:51] Marcus: On quantization — do you support Q4, Q8, or 3-bit? We care about inference cost.
[05:58] Priya: Runtime supports int4 and int8 pathways for many model formats; q3 is experimental. We will propose quantization profiles per model to balance quality and cost. The benchmark sheet will show delta in perplexity and latency.
[06:12] Samir: About latency — our interactive UI target is p95 < 250ms for 256-token completions. Is that realistic on Dedicated?
[06:22] Priya: It's plausible depending on model and hardware. Smaller, optimized models on A100/HTX or newer accelerator can meet that. But larger 70B+ models with long context usually push p95 higher. We can provide maps: config -> expected p95 per 1k tokens.
[06:38] Diane: We're also concerned about rollback and versioning for model updates — we need canary and A/B testing capabilities.
[06:45] Riley: Redwood Console supports rollouts, canaries, A/B, and automatic fallback to smaller models on SLO breach. We'll surface token-level cost and latency in the console.
[06:57] Ellen: On auditability — who can access inference logs? We need fine-grained RBAC.
[07:03] Priya: RBAC is supported, and logs can be shipped to your SIEM via secure sinks. We can limit token exposure and redact PII if needed.
[07:15] Diane: For the pilot, we'd like three configurations: 1) fast low-cost path for UI (quantized 13B-ish), 2) high-quality 70B-ish for accuracy, and 3) long-context pipeline for full-visit bundles. Can Redwood help stitch results?
[07:33] Priya: Absolutely. We'll set up a benchmark to run the three configs across your prompt set and multilingual samples. We'll show latency, token cost, and some QA metrics.
[07:45] Marcus: Network-wise, if we pick Dedicated, what peering options exist? VPC peering, PrivateLink?
[07:51] Riley: We support VPC peering in major clouds and PrivateLink where available. For Private on-prem, we support an air-gapped package.
[07:59] Ellen: Any residual data retention? We need guarantees on log retention and the ability to purge.
[08:06] Priya: We support configurable retention and deletion APIs; for Private you control retention. For Hosted/Dedicated we have retention policies and can set custom retention for enterprise contracts.
[08:18] Diane: About evaluation — what's a reasonable prompt set size for an initial run?
[08:23] Priya: 200-500 representative prompts across short interactive, long-doc summarization, and multilingual cases gives a good signal. For throughput/latency testing, a larger synthetic load helps.
[08:34] Samir: We'll compile that.
[08:37] Riley: Pricing note — we'll include Reserved Dedicated cost scenarios and per-token hosted estimates. We won't finalize pricing until we define throughput and model choices in the benchmark.
[08:48] Diane: Are there customers in healthcare doing similar long-context extraction?
[08:51] Riley: Yes, a few healthcare customers run long-context summarization and M* named ones — (audio overlap) — we'll include anonymized case studies.
[08:59] Marcus: One technical question: how does Redwood handle KV cache across requests when using streaming? We need session continuity across short interactions.
[09:07] Priya: We maintain session-level KV caches with TTL controls; streaming doesn't break cache continuity. For Dedicated and Private you can tune cache eviction and memory sizing.
[09:18] Diane: When you say tune, who's doing that — us or Redwood?
[09:21] Priya: We advise on defaults; for Dedicated we can co-manage tuning during the pilot. For Private you can self-manage with our tooling.
[09:33] Ellen: For compliance I'll need to see the SOC2 report and a network architecture diagram showing KMS and logging flows.
[09:40] Riley: Noted. We'll attach SOC2 and diagram as part of the security pack.
[09:45] Diane: Can we try a short proof: run 50 long-doc summarizations and 200 UI calls across 3 models?
[09:53] Priya: That's doable as a pilot. We'll run parallel batches and synthetic loads.
[09:58] Samir: Any known gotchas with tool-calling to internal services? We need retry semantics.
[10:04] Priya: Use idempotency keys and a broker layer for write operations; Redwood's runtimes provide hooks for pre/post-processing so you can validate before committing.
[10:14] Diane: Final question — vendor lock-in concerns. If we move models later, how portable is the stack?
[10:20] Riley: We emphasize portability: model artifacts in standard formats, config-as-code for routing, and exportable logs. Private mode gives the most portability.
[10:29] Ellen: OK. From risk perspective, we'll want a clause about data residency and a right-to-audit for the pilot contract.
[10:36] Riley: We'll work with legal on that.
[10:40] Priya: For next steps, we'll prepare the benchmark sheet with three model configs and an initial expected latency/cost table, plus the security pack. We'll propose a pilot scope for 4 weeks.
[10:51] Diane: Sounds good. Let's lock dates after we see the benchmark.
[10:56] Riley: Great. I'll send notes and follow-ups. Anything else?
[11:00] Ellen: No, that's it from security for now.
[11:03] Samir: No, thanks.
[11:05] Riley: Thanks everyone, end meeting.

Notes on transcription: there were a few overlaps and some product names misheard by the auto transcription (eg. some model names spelled phonetically). We preserved core decisions and owners.
